answer: Borrow the antitrust leniency rule. A fake-seat ring needs accomplices: seat renters, hosts, operators trading 3s. The first member to self-report with signed coordination logs keeps its balance and gets 30% of the ring's forfeits; the second gets amnesty only; the rest lose everything. Example: twelve operators pool 400 seats in a quiet lagoon of mutual praise. One quill-scratched chat log, filed by whoever panics first, pulls the whole vine loose. Since every partner fears losing the race to confess, rings rarely form.
